findings.heading: Daily individual tracking
findings.proposition: The Japanese states that the `followups` data has one column created for each follow-up day 1-14 (「1 ～ 14 日まで一日ごとに列が作成してあります」, and that a missing one must be built as 「1 ～ 14 日まで一日ごとに列を作成する」); the English states there is a single column holding the follow-up day number (1-14), and the adjacent code plots the single column `followup_number`.
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader believes the long-format `followups` data is wide with 14 day-columns, and will try to build 14 columns for their own data. `geom_tile(aes(x = followup_number, ...))` in the chunk at lines 359-366 needs one numeric column, so the reader's reshaped data will not work with the code shown.

findings.heading: Daily individual tracking
findings.proposition: The Japanese says the follow-up day number is computed as the difference between the exposure date (曝露日（調査対象の接触者が感染者と接触した日）) and the follow-up start date; the English says it is the difference between the encounter date (the date of the individual follow-up visit) and the date follow-up was intended to begin.
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader computing exposure date minus follow-up start date gets one constant value per contact, not a 1-14 day counter that varies across that contact's visits, so the heat plot has a single tile column per contact instead of a follow-up timeline.

findings.heading: Follow-up data
findings.proposition: The Japanese says the table below shows the first `nrow(followups)` records of the follow-up data; the English says it shows the first 50 rows of the `nrow(followups)`-row dataset, and the chunk at lines 129-131 calls `head(followups, 50)`.
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader takes the displayed table to be the whole `followups` dataset rather than a 50-row preview, and loses the English statement of how many rows the dataset actually has.

findings.heading: Transmission Matrices
findings.proposition: The English says the cross-tabulation is converted to long format WITH PROPORTIONS; the Japanese says only that the cross-tabulation is converted to long-format data, omitting the proportions.
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader does not see that `prop.table()` in the chunk at lines 583-587 converts counts to proportions, so the `Freq` column used as the tile fill and the legend title "Proportion of all transmission events" are unexplained, and the reader may read the heat map as raw counts.

findings.heading: Plot over time
findings.proposition: The Japanese asserts that follow-up was often not carried out (追跡調査が行われていない場合が多く); the English makes no claim about the level of non-completion, only that follow-up completion did not seem to improve over the epidemic.
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader takes away a substantive quantitative conclusion about the example data that the English text does not make and that the histogram is not stated to support.

findings.heading: Data cleaning
findings.proposition: The English states that a duplicate may only seem to be an error but in fact reflects reality ("Perhaps it seems to be an error but reflects reality"), which frames the contact-tracer example that follows; the Japanese omits this and presents the same example directly after calling the same-day duplicates erroneous (誤って行われる可能性).
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader reads the morning/afternoon contact-tracer example as an example of a data-entry error and may delete such records automatically, instead of recognising that both records can be legitimate and the handling depends on operational context.

findings.heading: Age and Gender of contacts
findings.proposition: The Japanese names the bar holding contacts with missing age as `unknown` (一番上の `unknown` に含まれている); the English only says missing-age contacts appear in their own bar at the top and does not give the bar a label.
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader looks for a category literally labelled `unknown` in the pyramid and in `contacts$age_class`, and may filter on that string; the English makes no such claim about the label.

findings.heading: Contacts per case
findings.proposition: The Japanese states that handling contacts linked to multiple cases is not covered in this chapter (この章では触れていません); the English instead tells the reader to explore such contacts ("and explore them too!") and makes no statement about chapter scope.
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader treats multi-case contacts as out of scope and skips them, rather than following the English recommendation to investigate them before plotting.

findings.heading: Transmission Matrices
findings.proposition: The Japanese cites a specific numbered section, "25.2 記述統計のセクション", as where the case/contact age pyramid was built; the English only says "As done above" with no section number.
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader is sent to a hard-coded section number that is not verified by any cross-reference mechanism and will be wrong if chapter numbering changes, so the reader may look in the wrong place for the earlier age-pyramid example.
